\section{At a Glance}
Owner brief (2026-09-27): ``also do a three phase motor driver''. This is a 3-phase BLDC driver designed from a general spec. The only reference was a published demo board seen in one frame of a short video; no spec, schematic or parts list was published for it, so every figure below is ours, and the guesses we made from the frame are listed as A1--A12 in \texttt{requirements.md}.

\begin{itemize}
\item VM 10--28 V (12--24 V nominal); 10 A RMS per phase continuous and 20 A peak, no heatsink (both provisional).
\item Six 60 V NTMFS5C628NL FETs; DRV8300D gate driver on a 12 V gate rail boosted from 5 V, bootstrapped high sides at about 11 V at any bus voltage.
\item 3 mOhm 2512 low-side shunts with Kelvin taps (net ties) into three INA240A1 amplifiers; STM32G431 for FOC.
\item Correctness first (gate loop, Kelvin sensing, power loop, thermal), then size. Stop at a DRC/ERC-clean fab package. Nothing ordered.
\end{itemize}

\section{What To Know Before Trusting It}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Gate drive.} The 12 V boost rail keeps high-side drive near 11 V from VM = 10 V up to the 45 V clamp; a charge-pump driver (DRV8320H) was rejected because it guarantees only 6.3 V at 10 V. Firmware must cap duty near 95\% for the bootstrap capacitors.
\item \textbf{Current sensing.} Kelvin taps start at each shunt's own pads through net ties. The INA240's inputs sit 5.4 mm apart on opposite pad rows, so each sense pair runs about 9 mm uncoupled against a 3 mm target; that is set by the packages and was waived with the owner's approval.
\item \textbf{Power loop and thermal.} Per-leg 3 x 10 uF + 100 nF across each leg, solid GND (In1) and VM (In2) planes, via fields at the drains and shunt returns. The board total is estimated at about 3.4 W at 10 A RMS; that is an estimate, not a simulation or a measurement. The two 470 uF cans are probably under-rated for the ripple at 10 A continuous.
\item \textbf{Waivers.} The design checks pass with 390 waivers: current 359 (mostly GND stitching and signal-current taps), creepage 24 (inside U301's and U101's courtyards per IPC-2221B A6, or between nets of the same phase leg), current-sense pairs 6 and one power-distribution artifact. Placement has 14 more.
\item \textbf{Necks.} 109 narrow power stubs were turned into same-shape copper zones to clear the track-width rule. The necks are not wider than before.
\item \textbf{Size.} 78 x 78 mm against a guessed 60 x 60 mm for the reference board: we put loop area and copper for heat first.
\item \textbf{Status.} Nothing has been built, measured or ordered.
\end{itemize}
